newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- BIDS UP AS NEW ISSUES PRICE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- BIDS UP AS NEW ISSUES PRICE.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were showing strength in early trade Tuesday, with the focus on a heavy new issue calendar.
"It's mostly flat. We're just getting started here," one trader said. "Once we get some (pricing) scales that may give the market a little bit of direction."
A second trader judged the bid-side up about three basis points, but the offered side was basically unchanged.
The government long bond, meanwhile, was up 14/32 to 97, pushing the yield down to 6.61 percent.
Muni market players said the large new issue calendar and several key July economic data releases this week continue to be the focus.
In early pricings, Goldman Sachs & Co said it tentatively priced $371 million Denver Airport bonds at a top yield of 5.60 percent in 2025.

Smith Barney Inc said it tentatively priced a two-part $442 million New York City Metropolitan Transportation Authority issue. The agency's $277 million commuter facilities bonds came at a 5.56 percent top yield in 2027, while $165 million of transit facilities bonds carried a 5.625 percent top yield in 2027.

On the competitive side, 26 sales totaling $681 million were scheduled. A $267 million Portland, Ore., refunding offering at 1300 was the largest, followed by a $141 million Delaware Transportation Authority deal at 1100 EDT.

Futures prices were also higher early Tuesday, with September municipals up 8/32 to 119-6/32. September T-bonds gained 12/32 to 113-4/32, moving the MOB spread to 194 ticks from 198 at the close on Monday.

In muni secondary action, bids on Dade County, Fla., FGIC water and sewer 5-1/4s of 2026 were unchanged from Monday at 5.54 percent. Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5.0s of 2024 were one basis points lower, at 5.54 percent.
In economic data Tuesday, The Atlanta Federal Reserve said its July business activity index rose to 23.3, compared to June's downwardly revised reading of 15.3.
In other news, BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales survey said sales for the week of August 9 fell 0.5 percent from the prior week.
But market participants said the key data would come later in the week, with July retail sales and last month's inflation data hitting the market on Wednesday and Thursday.
